title: Fonts
summary: A magazine type cabinet: condensed and Didone high-contrast serifs with true italics for headlines, mastheads and numerals, clean grotesques for small tracked labels and captions, and a mono for folios and figures. All bundled locally with open licences (SIL OFL 1.1, from google/fonts).
usage: The theme sets headlines in Instrument Serif (sentence case, tight leading) and the one accent word in Instrument Serif Italic; mastheads and huge numerals in Bodoni Moda; small labels in Inter Tight 600 capitals tracked .2em; folios, timecodes and table figures in DM Mono. Newsreader, Fraunces, Playfair Display and DM Serif Display are alternates for display; Hanken Grotesk, Archivo, Manrope and DM Sans for text. Kit names: F.head, F.italic, F.serif, F.sans, F.mono.

items.note: Theme headline face: condensed, high contrast, so long headlines stay large in a narrow vertical frame. Sentence case.
The accent: the one word that matters, in the surface's accent colour. Written *like this* in text props.
Didone for mastheads, drop caps and big numerals: vertical stress, hairline serifs. Large sizes only.
Didone italic for ampersands, issue numbers and large pull-quote marks.
Theme label face: small capitals tracked .2em at 600; sentence-case UI text at 500.
Medium weight of the folio face, for figures on footage.
Wider news serif alternate: sturdier at small sizes, for standfirsts and longer quotes.
Its italic, for longer emphasised passages.
Soft old-style alternate with more warmth; good at heavy weights for a friendlier cover line.
Transitional display alternate with strong bold weights.
Heavier display serif for a single short word that must hold on busy footage.
Warmer grotesque alternate for labels and captions.
Grotesque with a width axis; heavy weights for a bold sans cover line beside the serif.
Light modern sans for sentence-case credits.
Quiet low-contrast sans for longer lines.
